topics.title: Why Economics? Economic activities and economic agents

concepts.learning_objective: Identify economic activities as those undertaken for monetary gain, the 'ordinary business of life'.
Distinguish consumer, seller, producer, employee and employer by the role a person plays.

topics.title: Scarcity, alternative uses and the problem of choice

concepts.learning_objective: Explain scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants as the root of all economic problems.
Explain how alternative uses of limited resources give rise to the problem of choice.

topics.title: Consumption, production, distribution and the scope of economics

concepts.learning_objective: Classify an economic question as a study of consumption, production or distribution.
Explain why modern economics includes special studies such as poverty and disparity, which need statistics.

topics.title: Statistics in economics: data, analysis and policies

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise economic facts as economic data needed to analyse economic problems.
Relate the analysis of causes of an economic problem to the formulation of policies.

topics.title: What is statistics? Quantitative and qualitative data

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of statistics and the stages of a statistical study.
Distinguish quantitative data from qualitative data (attributes).

topics.title: What statistics does: functions and limits

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how statistics makes facts precise and condenses mass data into summary measures.
Explain the use of statistics in finding economic relationships, predicting trends and framing policy.
Evaluate the misuse of statistical measures and why they are no substitute for common sense.
